analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction about being charged foreign transaction fees on the Harbourline Travel Card and about how he was treated by an agent on the phone, alleging financial loss of £18.40 and distress, which meets CH-1.
analysis.summary: Customer holds the Harbourline Travel Card and was charged £18.40 in foreign transaction fees while in Lisbon. The card should not carry these fees. Staff note confirms six FX fees totalling £18.40 were charged because the tariff was set up wrongly on the account. When the customer phoned about it on 21/10 he waited 50 minutes and says the agent was short with him and ended the call. He wants the fees refunded and an apology for how he was treated. A call recording from 21/10 has been requested. No vulnerability was recorded in the handler note.

timeline.event: Customer phoned about the foreign transaction fees; waited 50 minutes, agent was short and ended the call (per customer)
Complaint received by phone; handler confirmed six FX fees totalling £18.40 caused by incorrect tariff set-up; call recording from 21/10 requested

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss of £18.40 falls under £100, which would be Low under CH-6. Medium is set because the complaint includes an allegation of staff conduct (agent being short and ending the call), and CH-6 classes complaints about staff conduct as Medium.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None indicated in the case file. Handler note records no vulnerability. Consider confirming no support needs if the customer's circumstances change.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger applies. The fee arises from an incorrect tariff set-up, which is a bank error, and there is no fraud, lending, vulnerability referral, systemic issue, legal threat, or systems investigation recorded. The complaints handler can resolve it. The tariff error may need checking for other Harbourline Travel Card customers, which the handler may wish to consider.

policy_citations.quote: Foreign transaction fees are not charged on the Harbourline Travel Card. Any such fee on that card is a bank error and FEE-2 applies.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer was charged foreign transaction fees on the Harbourline Travel Card, which this clause says should not happen. The fees are therefore a bank error, and FEE-2 applies to them.

policy_citations.quote: Where a fee was charged because of a bank error (for example a system fault, an incorrect tariff or a payment the bank failed to process on time), the fee must be refunded in full, together with any interest charged on it, plus a goodwill payment in line with policy RED.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The handler note says the tariff was set up wrongly, which is an incorrect tariff example of bank error. Refund of the fees, any interest, and a goodwill payment should be considered by the handler. The amount and decision are for the handler to make.

policy_citations.quote: Medium: financial loss between £100 and £1,000, repeated service failure (the customer has contacted us three or more times about the same issue), or a complaint about staff conduct.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The complaint includes an allegation about agent conduct during the call, so Medium severity applies.

policy_citations.quote: Every complaint must be tagged with one primary root cause from the approved list: Fees and charges;
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The primary complaint is about foreign transaction fees, so the root cause is Fees and charges.
